newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Police clash with strikers near Buenos Aires.
newsitem.headline: Police clash with strikers near Buenos Aires.

text.p: Argentine police fired rubber bullets at stone-throwing strikers in the grimy western outskirts of Buenos Aires Thursday, leaving at least seven injured, local media reported.

A few dozen protestors manning a roadblock in the poor Isidro Casanova neighborhood poured gasoline on the ground and set it alight and local television showed police in riot gear charging, with a hail of stones bouncing off their shields.

Six demonstrators were hurt by rubber bullets and one policeman was taken to the hospital after being hit by a stone, the private DyN news agency reported. Most of the protestors fled down nearby streets, but police arrested two.
The CTA and MTA opposition unions called the 24-hour general strike to protest against 16.1 percent unemployment and proposed labor market reforms.
The strike has been most effective in poorer provinces, and business in the capital, Buenos Aires, has mainly carried on as usual. But about 20 roadblocks have been set up throughout the country.
